fixes.explanation: That's the one, friend. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says a wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son grief to his mother. Either way, the son's choices land on the people who love him. Nobody's choices stay in their own little corner.

Not quite, friend. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), says a wise son brings joy to his father, and a foolish son brings grief to his mother. Joy and grief both land on somebody else. If a son's choices only touched himself, nobody's face would light up or fall.

That one adds more than the verse says. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (Proverbs 1:1), only tells us that a wise son brings joy to his father and a foolish son grief to his mother. The proverb never says who decides how he turns out. I'll stick with what's on the page, friend, and the page says a son's choices reach his parents.
Righteousness is the answer, baker! The verse says it flat out: "…righteousness brings deliverance from death." Treasure gotten the wrong way profits nothing, but righteousness actually delivers.

Generosity is a lovely guess, friend, and I'd never talk you out of being generous. But Solomon doesn't put it in this line. He says, "…righteousness brings deliverance from death." That's the word to hold onto.

Let me read you what Solomon really says, friend: "The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but He denies the craving of the wicked." That's the opposite of what the card said. The LORD is the one who doesn't let the righteous go hungry. It's an easy one to flip, and I've flipped plenty of recipes the same way.

Not that one, friend, because the verse goes the other direction. Solomon says, "…but love covers all transgressions." Hatred is the one stirring up dissension. Love works the opposite way and covers.

You spotted it, friend! The mouth and the lips keep showing up in these proverbs: the mouth of the wicked, foolish lips, the mouth of the righteous, the mouth of the fool. Mouths and lips are for speaking, so Solomon keeps his eye on what people say.

That's right, friend. Solomon says the labor of the righteous leads to life, and the gain of the wicked brings punishment. He follows the labor of one and the gain of the other to where each ends up. Life on one side, punishment on the other.

Let's reread it together, friend. Solomon says, "Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray." The one who ignores reproof doesn't stay on the path, he goes astray. The path to life is the one for whoever heeds instruction.

Right, friend. Solomon says, "Whoever heeds instruction is on the path to life, but he who ignores reproof goes astray." So the one who ignores reproof goes astray. Whoever heeds instruction is the one on the path to life.

Judgment is right, baker. Solomon says, "The lips of the righteous feed many, but fools die for lack of judgment." The righteous feed many with their lips, while fools die for lack of judgment. It's a hard line, but it's a clear one.

Right, friend. Solomon says, "The blessing of the LORD enriches, and He adds no sorrow to it." The blessing enriches, and the LORD adds no sorrow to it. That's why the second half of the card doesn't match the verse.

The slacker, you got it! Solomon says, "Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him." Vinegar on your teeth, smoke in your eyes, that's what the slacker is to the ones who sent him. Ouch, what a picture.

The mocker is a good guess, friend, but it's not the word in this verse. Solomon says, "Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the slacker to those who send him." The one he names is the slacker.

Gossip is a good guess in a chapter full of lips, friend, but this verse has someone else in mind. Solomon says, "…so is the slacker to those who send him." Vinegar and smoke are what the slacker is to the ones who sent him.
